 Kenrich Williams 
 OKC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #34 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Kenrich Williams finished Saturday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers.
 After totaling 10 points in his first two starts of the season, Williams scored 11 on Saturday. He was most valuable against the Rockets in three-pointers and rebounds, but this performance doesn’t make “Kenny Hustle” a must-add heading into Oklahoma City’s four-game Week 3. Also, with the Thunder playing two games against Cleveland to start the week, it’s fair to wonder whether head coach Mark Daigneault would consider a bigger lineup to match up with Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. If so, Williams or Jared McCain (10/4/2/1) could be headed to the bench. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Monday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Although Jared McCain is available for Monday’s game, the Thunder are starting with a bigger lineup. JayWill has replaced him, which should help the Thunder match up better against Cleveland’s Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. 
 Chet Holmgren 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #7 
 According to ESPN’s Tim MacMahon, Chet Holmgren (knee) will be sidelined for at least 8-10 weeks. 
 According to MacMahon, Holmgren underwent a biological treatment on Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear in his right knee. With Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) facing extended absences, and given Holmgren’s injury history, fantasy managers should expect the Thunder to be very cautious with his rehab process. Kenrich Williams should remain in the starting lineup for the foreseeable future, and Aday Mara’s playing time should increase. Also, Holmgren’s absence raises Isaiah Hartenstein’s fantasy ceiling. 
 Chet Holmgren 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #7 
 Chet Holmgren (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Unfortunately, Holmgren sitting out Monday’s win over the Suns wasn’t solely because it was Oklahoma City’s second game in as many nights. Kenrich Williams moved into the starting lineup and played 24 minutes against Phoenix; he should fill a similar role on Wednesday. 
 Jared McCain 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Jared McCain tallied 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns. 
 McCain was one of three replacements in the Thunder starting lineup on Monday. With Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) needing surgery, McCain has a good chance of staying a starter for the long haul. He shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc against the Suns and recorded a complete stat line, playing 30 minutes. Like Ajay Mitchell, McCain is a must-add if he’s on the waiver wire. 
 Jared McCain 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 The Thunder have three new starters for Monday’s game, and two (McCain and Mitchell) could hold onto those roles for the foreseeable future. Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) could miss the rest of the season due to injuries that require surgery. “Kenny Hustle” starts for Chet Holmgren, who is dealing with right patellar tendinitis. 
 Jalen Williams 
 OKC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #8 
 Jalen Williams has suffered a fractured fibula and a dislocated ankle. 
 Williams’s injury was gruesome, and this diagnosis confirms it. General manager Sam Presti said a timeline will be provided following the surgery, but at this time, it’s unclear exactly how long he’ll be out. However, given the severity, it’s safe to say it will be a lengthy absence for him. Jared McCain and Ajay Mitchell should both take on larger roles with Cason Wallace (shoulder) set to undergo surgery as well. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell accounted for 18 points (8-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Clippers. 
 The Thunder lost Cason Wallace (shoulder) in the first quarter on Sunday. While Mitchell wasn’t the choice to start the third quarter, his role will expand if Wallace misses time. Jared McCain (three points, one rebound, one steal, and one three-pointer) replaced Wallace, and he can provide points and three-pointers in that role. However, Mitchell is the better option for fantasy managers left choosing between the two on the waiver wire. 
 Jared McCain 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Jared McCain provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (7-of-9 FGs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and six three-pointers against the Spurs on Tuesday. 
 McCain was on fire from beyond the arc in this game and was able to spark some runs for the Thunder. He matched his career high for three-pointers in a game, which he also did twice during the first month of his rookie season. McCain was an excellent addition for the Thunder last season, and he’s going to continue to make an impact off the bench this year. However, managers shouldn’t be rushing to the waiver wire after this since he likely won’t have performances of this magnitude consistently. 
 Jared McCain 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Jared McCain led the Thunder with 20 points (6-of-13 FGs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and six three-pointers in a 114-112 overtime win over the Pacers on Tuesday. 
 McCain led Oklahoma City in scoring in just 19 minutes in the overtime win. Sam Presti already hyped him up before the preseason began, and he has shown why during the preseason, having now hit 13 triples across three games. When the team is fully healthy, his role will likely be too limited for him to make an impact for fantasy managers, but it should be large enough for him to be an important piece in OKC’s rotation. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Thunder general manager Sam Presti names Cason Wallace, Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain as players that will play more minutes this season. 
 Not only will all three take on larger roles with Luguentz Dort now in Atlanta, but Presti is expecting genuine jumps in their production. All 3 players had strong stretches for OKC last season, and they’ll be relied on once again to help the Thunder get back on track after losing in the Western Conference Finals last season. Wallace seems like the most likely choice to start, but Mitchell and McCain will play big minutes off the bench.
